audit.whatIsWrong: Every full-layer row read 'Skill' while the content layer read LeBlanc for rows 0-5 and Swain for row 6 — seven rows of cross-layer disagreement.
audit.why: 53.31% over 1300 games with a clear shape: LeBlanc bursts him before Ravenous Flock and sustain items matter, and Swain takes over once his ultimate is draining a whole fight. The content layer and the packet already agreed on that shape; the full layer was the stale one.
audit.corrected: phases[0-5].side set to LeBlanc, phases[6].side to Swain, and phases[6].why rewritten so the row and its sentence agree.

audit.why: Swain's spikes are 6 (Demonic Ascension, flat 120s) and sustain items; LeBlanc's are 3, 6 and first item. spikes[2] now names the anti-heal timing that decides the first-item window.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds folded into spikes[2] and the late text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The root was attributed to Vision of Empire (W). Vision of Empire is the global eye — 22/21/20/19/18s, 5500 to 7500 range — that damages, slows and reveals. The root is Nevermove (E), 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s at 850. The page also called Demonic Ascension a channel to outlast.
audit.why: Nevermove roots on the wave's RETURN trip, not the outgoing throw, and Swain can then pull every rooted champion toward him — into the 650 drain. That two-beat timing is the whole dodge, and the page never mentioned it. Demonic Ascension has no duration to wait out: it persists as long as he keeps draining champions.
audit.corrected: Root reattributed to Nevermove with the return-trip timing and the pull; Vision of Empire restated; the 'ult channel completes' advice replaced.

audit.why: Nevermove's 12s-to-10s is the step-up clock; R is a flat 120s regardless of rank, which is worth counting exactly.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal appeared only as 'his sustain' in itemization and never in the content layer.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock heals him from Soul Fragments and permanently raises his maximum health, so waiting makes the burst maths worse every minute.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds named in spikes[2] and late.

edits.after: Levels 3-6 your full combo still kills him outright if you dodge Nevermove's return, and Mimic-Chain plus a well-timed all-in denies him the setup entirely. Respect the pull, though: rooted champions get dragged toward him, and Demonic Ascension keeps running as long as a champion stays inside its 650 radius.

edits.before: Once Swain has sustain items and his ultimate draining a full teamfight, he becomes extremely hard to actually kill — the healing outpaces your burst and he anchors fights from the backline. Focus picks before teamfights start, or burn him down before his ult channel completes.
edits.after: Once Swain has sustain items and his ultimate draining a full teamfight, he is extremely hard to kill — the healing outpaces your burst and he anchors the fight. Demonic Ascension is not a channel you can outlast: it runs as long as he drains champions, so take the pick before the fight starts and bring Grievous Wounds.

notes: Full layer read 'Skill' on all seven rows while content read LeBlanc x6 + Swain; aligned the full layer to the content layer and the packet, so no win[N] edits were needed (proposing them would have been no-ops with before == after). Main kit fix: the root is Nevermove (E), not Vision of Empire (W), and it roots on the return trip with a follow-up pull. Also removed 'before his ult channel completes' — Demonic Ascension has no fixed duration while he is draining champions. Note for the data owner: the Ravenous Flock kit entry carries a percentHealth flag, but Riot's description only mentions healing and permanent max-health growth, so I wrote only the anti-heal case and did not assert percent-health damage.
